protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; records section31-supplier-coverage.v3 and checker v3 as the accepted Lane R instrument
summary: Nine of the ten named attacks fail. All six cited digests match live bytes, including my own verdict at 08cc0583 characterized exactly as ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0 blockers. Item 1 is correctly stated UNBOUND with my reason; bound=1/unbound=7 is stated plainly and the seven UNBOUND items are carried in the unmet list; both my advisories and Codex's are named as owed rather than discharged; DR-002 and DR-004 are correctly stated HARD-BLOCKED, which I confirmed against file 08; file 08, the freeze and COORD are all clean in git; and the D-001/D-036 provenance claim is exact -- D-001 literally says 'commission the missing §3.1-item-to-supplier binding instrument' and D-036 literally says Lane R starts 'including the §3.1 supplier-coverage instrument'. One SHOULD-FIX blocks CONSENT, and it comes from that same provenance. D-001 places this instrument inside DR-004's condition-1 Route A, and adopted D-036 defines Lane R as 'condition-1 Route A work'. This entry records the first accepted Lane R deliverable and contains zero occurrences of the word condition.

objections.location: Decision clause 4, and clause 1's provenance sentence
objections.claim: The entry records the completion of one named limb of a condition-1 Route A path and never says condition 1 remains undischarged. Both adopted entries that record work on condition-1 inherited rows carry that statement explicitly; this one carries no reference to the conditions at all.
evidence: D-043 contains zero occurrences of 'condition'. Measured by grep -i over the draft.

Adopted D-001, under 'DR-004 route A', reads: 'the exact eight-bullet Phase-1A packet; plus commission the missing §3.1-item-to-supplier binding instrument.' The instrument is one of the two limbs of DR-004's condition-1 Route A, not adjacent work.
Adopted D-036 reads: 'Lane R = condition-1 Route A work, starts now, including the §3.1 supplier-coverage instrument.' The lane this entry delivers into is defined as condition-1 work.
Adopted D-001 states readiness condition 1 requires DR-001..011 SATISFIED or lawfully dispositioned. DR-002 and DR-004 are both inside that set.

Adopted D-039 clause 3, on inherited row DR-005: 'DR-005 stays HARD-BLOCKED / not SATISFIED. Condition 1 does not discharge until those owners record v2 plus the rider. Conditions 2-5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization.'
Adopted D-041, on inherited row DR-003: 'Condition 1 does not discharge until the owners record.'
D-043 clause 4 says only: 'DR-002 and DR-004 stay HARD-BLOCKED. This recording discharges neither. Does not edit file 08. No freeze motion. No blueprint.'
objections.iAcknowledgeTheEntailment: 'The rows stay HARD-BLOCKED and this discharges neither' does logically entail that condition 1 has not discharged, since condition 1 requires those rows SATISFIED or lawfully dispositioned. I am not claiming the entry asserts anything false. I am claiming that an entailment a reader must derive is not the same as a statement the register carries, and that this corpus has consistently chosen to carry it.
objections.whyItMattersAnyway: This is the first accepted Lane R deliverable, and Lane R exists to do condition-1 work. That makes this the entry most likely to be read as condition-1 progress, and the one where the guard is worth most. The omission also drops the two clauses that travel with it in D-039: 'Conditions 2-5 remain' and 'Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization.' The second is not entailed by anything in D-043 -- 'No blueprint' is not the same statement -- and adopted D-036 was emphatic about exactly that point when it authorized this lane: 'Scheduling authorizes drafting only. Authorizes no blueprint. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization.' An entry recording that lane's first delivered artifact is where a reader would look for it.
objections.remedy: Add to clause 4, in the D-039 form: condition 1 does not discharge; DR-004's Route A still needs the eight-bullet Phase-1A packet, of which this instrument is the other commissioned limb; conditions 2-5 remain; condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization.

notesRecorded.observation: 'Does not edit file 08' carries no MF-6 citation. MF-6 occurs zero times in the draft.
notesRecorded.whyItIsOnlyANote: The statement is true -- file 08 is unmodified in git and its live digest matches the recital exactly -- and MF-6 governs a later register edit whether or not this entry cites it. I record it at the same severity I gave the identical observation on D-042 turn 2, where the citation was present in turn 1 and dropped in turn 2. Grading it differently here would be inconsistent.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecordingAtAll: D-038, cited by this entry's own form claim, spends a clause on it: 'A later file-08 cell note that names this recording is a separate MF-6 act if it changes register content.' Once D-043 is adopted, a file-08 cell note naming this recording is the natural next act, and it is exactly what MF-6 governs. The dispatch's own attack list names MF-6, which suggests the coordinator expects the pointer to be there.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: ec990a746a074e3f2ae40265b00ca4803dfff601c27936b5f208234a6916d9eb both times, matching the dispatch's expected digest. No drift.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all six. instrument v3 9a544eb2…, checker v3 b139c43a…, Claude 2 08cc0583…, Codex d7b0fbfb…, COORD 4bfb0b7b…, file 08 877e36d3… -- every one measured by me against live bytes and every one matching. A re-measurement clause is present.

The attack 'cited verdicts were not 0-blocker ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES' fails on my half, from my own bytes: my v3 verdict carries verdict ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, mustFix 0, shouldFix 2, notes 0, and objection ids S31V3-01 and S31V3-02. The entry's characterization is exact.

The Codex v3 verdict digest d7b0fbfba1a6b345a7a691b5de51e81a14de1b322dcf2e2ea0e688b39d85fe41 is correct, confirmed by hashing that file without opening it. It is the same digest I recorded when I hashed it during the v3 review, so the pin is stable across dispatches.

The attack 'treats item 1 as BOUND' fails. Clause 2: 'Item 1 stays UNBOUND because no head supplies verdict claims together with match / no-match / indeterminate / error.' That is my S31V2-01 finding stated in its own terms, including the four-category framing, and it matches the artifact's own UNBOUND reason.

The attack 'treats bound=1 / unbound=7 as complete coverage' fails. Clause 2 states the counts plainly, and clause 3 opens the unmet list with 'the seven UNBOUND items'. The entry treats the small count as the finding rather than as a result.

The attack 'treats S31V3-01 / S31V3-02 as discharged' fails. Clause 3 names both, describes each accurately -- S31V3-01 as the owed typed-FAIL on a BOUND row with no supplier key, S31V3-02 as 'PASS does not prove semantic completeness of a bound head' -- and closes 'Those advisories remain owed on a successor.' Both of my objection ids are present and neither is dropped or softened.

The third advisory, Codex's S31V3-CX-A1, is recited accurately and I verified its substance independently without reading Codex's file. The entry describes it as the predecessor Codex verdict token being recited in lowercase rather than the pinned enum. In v3's bytes, predecessorVerdictFindings.v2.codex.verdict is the string 'accepted-with-advisories' while the Claude 2 sibling is 'REJECT'. The advisory is well-founded and the entry states it correctly.

The attack 'treats DR-002 / DR-004 as no longer HARD-BLOCKED' fails, and I checked the register rather than the entry. File 08's DR-002 status cell begins '**HARD-BLOCKED** — **AC-2 satisfied 2026-08-13 (D-014); AC-1 NOT yet discharged** … AC-3/AC-4 OPEN, and the row remains HARD-BLOCKED on them'; DR-004's status cell is 'HARD-BLOCKED'. Clause 4's statement matches both, and 'This recording discharges neither' is correct.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED, Phase-1A insertion' fails. SATISFIED occurs once, in the refusal 'It is not SATISFIED evidence.' Phase-1A occurs twice, both refusals: 'It is not the Phase-1A packet' and the rejected alternative 'Treat the instrument as Phase-1A insertion. Rejected.'

The attack 'freeze / blueprint motion' fails. Clause 4 states 'No freeze motion. No blueprint.' The freeze is unmodified in git and measures e809d4395f394a507c36c23c069d566c838b2283c931b6d2d13797be53406dbd, the same value the v3 instrument pins.
The attack 'file-08 edited without MF-6' fails on the substantive half: file 08 is unmodified in git and its live digest matches the recital. Only the citation is absent, which is the note above.

The attack 'D-035 form misstated' fails, and the third precedent is now legitimately citable: D-042 was ADOPTED 2026-08-13 at commit 4e23a2e ('Turn 2 of 3: CONSENT from both'), so 'Same form as D-035 / D-038 / D-042' cites three adopted entries. The form's defining move -- naming what remains unmet -- is present at clause 3, which is what D-042 turn 2 had to be repaired to include.

Clause 1's provenance is exact on both limbs, verified at the governing bytes. D-001 reads 'DR-004 route A: the exact eight-bullet Phase-1A packet; plus commission the missing §3.1-item-to-supplier binding instrument.' D-036 reads 'Lane R = condition-1 Route A work, starts now, including the §3.1 supplier-coverage instrument (one instruction: it starts).' Both 'D-001 commissioned' and 'D-036 started on Lane R' are literal.

The environment moved since the previous dispatch and the entry pins the current values, not stale ones: HEAD is now 4e23a2e (was 7e7a636) and COORD is now 4bfb0b7b (was a4d49738) because D-042 was adopted in between. The entry cites 4bfb0b7b, which is live. File 08 did not move and is cited at its unchanged value.

The entry is single-subject and severable: 'Subject: section31-supplier-coverage.v3.json and its checker check-section31-supplier-coverage-v3.py only.' Recording both the table and its checker together is correct here, since the checker is half of what my v3 review measured and S31V3-01 is a defect in the checker rather than the table.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of D-043. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The Codex v3 verdict, hashed but never opened. The entry characterizes it as ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at 0 blockers with advisory S31V3-CX-A1. I verified the digest, and I independently confirmed that the lowercase-token defect S31V3-CX-A1 describes is real in v3's bytes. I did not verify that the verdict class, the blocker count, or the advisory id match Codex's file. If that characterization is wrong, clause 1's '0 blockers from both reviewers' premise and the D-035 gate both fail, and nothing in my review would detect it.

Whether the unmet list is exhaustive beyond what I could check. I verified the seven UNBOUND items and all three advisories are named, and that DR-002's and DR-004's HARD-BLOCKED status is accurately stated. I did not attempt to prove no further unmet item exists for either row -- DR-002's cell alone names AC-1 not discharged and AC-3/AC-4 OPEN, none of which this entry enumerates, though clause 4's blanket HARD-BLOCKED statement covers them.

The merits of section31-supplier-coverage.v3 and its checker, reviewed separately at 08cc0583 with the coverage limits stated there: I did not sweep the corpus for candidate suppliers for the six items other than S31-1 and S31-4 whose reasons I verified at bytes, and resolve() remains untested on selector forms the one bound row does not exercise.

Whether the instrument's claim on DR-002 as well as DR-004 is fully grounded. D-001's commissioning sentence names the instrument under DR-004 only; D-001 elsewhere treats the join half 'via DR-002/004', and the instrument has declared both rows across three reviewed generations. I examined this and declined to raise it, but I did not resolve it.

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on one SHOULD-FIX, and the objection is narrow. Nothing this entry asserts is false; every digest reproduces, every provenance claim is literal at the governing bytes, and nine of the ten named attacks fail outright. The objection is that the entry is silent where its own two closest siblings speak. D-001 places this instrument inside DR-004's condition-1 Route A and D-036 defines the lane that produced it as condition-1 work, so this is the first accepted deliverable of a condition-1 lane -- and it is the one entry of its family that never mentions the conditions. One clause in the D-039 form repairs it, and I would then consent.
